ready.description: User principle (2026-06-02): 'the cli shouldn't implement core logic. We'll need to break it up. It'll be a spike someday, maybe even today.' That (a) starts the breakup, (b) de-dups the 4 handlers, (c) is the natural home for the prx-hz1 deadline+reap+no-plan-mode fix, (d) gives prx-p1i a real boundary to assert.

ready.title: STRUCTURAL: global ~/.beads symlink at $HOME shadows every repo; per-repo 'bd init'/'prx repo bootstrap' refuses (no bd discovery-root boundary)
ready.acceptance_criteria:
- 'prx repo bootstrap <slug>' succeeds on a beads-less repo nested under $HOME even when a global ~/.beads exists, creating a per-repo workspace bound to io_github_<owner>_<repo> (NOT the global DB).
- bd workspace discovery is bounded to the repo/git root (via bd flag or prx pre-scaffold), so an ancestor ~/.beads no longer shadows per-repo init.
- The 'already-initialized' refusal no longer mis-advises 'prx repo backfill' when the discovered workspace is a global ancestor rather than a repo-local one.
- Regression: bootstrap test with a simulated ancestor .beads above the repo root.
ready.description:
THE blocker for 'use prx on all repos' (epic prx-47y). Found onboarding flask-mysql-ngrok.

MECHANISM (confirmed):
- ~/.beads is a symlink -> ~/.local/share/beads-home (global beads home with embeddeddolt + shared-server + legacy default.db).
- bd 1.0.3 resolves its workspace by walking UP the cwd directory path looking for a .beads. From any repo worktree under /Users/bobby (i.e. every repo), the walk-up reaches /Users/bobby/.beads and resolves the DB to ~/.local/share/beads-home/embeddeddolt.
- This walk-up is PATH-based, independent of $HOME. So prx's GH-1750 tempHome HOME-isolation (repo_bootstrap.ts:400-430) does NOT prevent it — it only masks bd's ${HOME}/.local/share/beads-home PROBE, not the cwd ancestor walk.
- Result: 'prx repo bootstrap <slug>' on a beads-less repo returns refusal 'bd-init-workspace-already-initialized' (repo_bootstrap.ts:451). bd init refuses to create a per-repo workspace because it 'already' sees the global one.
- bd init has NO flag to bound discovery to the git/repo root (verified: --database/--server/--stealth/--prefix/--non-interactive only).

WHY PRX ITSELF WORKS BUT NEW REPOS DON'T: prx ships a committed .beads/ at its worktree root (commit 1c7be1c). bd's walk-up stops at that local .beads before reaching ~/.beads. A fresh repo has no local .beads to shadow with, and bd refuses to create one — chicken-and-egg.

SECONDARY DEFECT: the refusal's remediation text tells the operator to run 'prx repo backfill <slug>' to record the EXISTING workspace's prefix. That is WRONG for this case — it would bind the new repo to the GLOBAL beads workspace/prefix instead of giving it its own io_github_<owner>_<repo> DB. The advice conflates 'this repo already has its own workspace' with 'a global ancestor workspace is shadowing this repo'.

CANDIDATE FIXES (decision needed):
(a) bd: bound workspace discovery to the git toplevel (stop walk-up at repo root / add --discovery-root or honor .git boundary). Cleanest; upstream bd change (external tool).
(b) prx bootstrap: scaffold a minimal repo-local .beads/ marker at the worktree root BEFORE invoking bd init, so the walk-up terminates at the repo root rather than $HOME. Keeps fix inside prx.
(c) remove/relocate the global ~/.beads symlink at $HOME (operator state change). Destructive to existing global beads; tooling explicitly warns against moving beads-home.
(d) pass bd init --database <canonical> --server --external and a cwd/root scoping so it targets the per-repo shared-server DB regardless of ancestor discovery — verify bd still refuses on ancestor presence.
ready.design:
FIX DESIGN (additive; only changes the currently-broken ancestor-shadowed path):

In prx repo bootstrap, BEFORE runBdInit:
1. Detect ancestor-shadowing: run 'bd where' from workspaceCwd; if the resolved .beads dir is NOT at/under the repo root (i.e. it's an ancestor like ~/.beads), the embedded bd init will abort. This is the trigger condition.
2. When shadowed: scaffold a repo-local .beads/metadata.json directly (shared-server shape: {database:dolt, backend:dolt, dolt_mode:server, dolt_database: canonicalDoltDatabase(origin), project_id}). This stops bd's walk-up at the repo root (PROVEN: bd where/info then resolve locally). Emit a new BD_BOOTSTRAP_BOUNDARY_SCAFFOLDED event. SKIP the embedded bd init (it would abort / create the wrong embedded mode); the workspace is now declared shared-server, matching this operator's real topology (~/.local/share/beads-home/shared-server exists; prx's own metadata is dolt_mode:server).
3. When NOT shadowed: unchanged — runBdInit embedded path as today.
4. Provisioning of the actual DB on the shared dolt server is the existing 'prx dolt provision' step (separate task prx-1hq), so scaffold need not create the DB.

OPEN IMPLEMENTATION QUESTIONS:
- project_id provenance: bd init generates a UUID; a manual scaffold needs one. Options: (a) generate via crypto.randomUUID(); (b) leave null and let provision/first bd write populate it; (c) derive deterministically from canonical DB. Need to confirm bd tolerates a scaffolded project_id (or absent).
- Mode default: this changes bootstrap to produce SHARED-SERVER for the shadowed case while the documented default is embedded per-project. Coherent for this operator (shared-server topology) but a behavior shift to confirm.

Smaller alternative (does NOT unblock onboarding): only fix the misleading refusal text (stop recommending 'prx repo backfill' for the ancestor-shadow case). Rejected as primary because the operator stays blocked.
ready.notes:
STRATEGIC UPDATE (bd-source agent + verification): the shadow is a bd-VERSION problem, likely fixable WITHOUT the prx scaffold workaround.
- Current bd main (commit 4e8cedc) BOUNDS the cwd walk-up at the git root via findGitRoot()/git.GetRepoRoot() (PR #1731, closing issue #1653). All our target repos ARE git repos.
- Installed bd 1.0.3 (dev) LACKS this: verified 'bd where' from flask's git worktree resolves to ~/.beads/embeddeddolt (ABOVE flask's git root). So 1.0.3 predates #1731.
=> LIKELY FIX: upgrade bd to a build with PR #1731. Then bd won't walk past a repo's git root to ~/.beads, dissolving the shadow for git repos. The prx-side scaffold-boundary workaround becomes UNNECESSARY for git repos (still needed only for non-git dirs, which onboarding doesn't use).
- Caveat from agent: even current main still has the non-git-cwd shadow (GetRepoRoot returns '' outside a repo); not relevant to onboarding.
- ~/.beads is the OPERATOR symlink -> ~/.local/share/beads-home (not a bd constant). 
NEXT: verify by upgrading bd + re-testing bd init from flask; if fixed, downgrade prx-zz4 / fold into 'upgrade bd' rather than ship a scaffold.

ready.title: feature: Make GitHub-issue tracking automatic (intake→gh + PR Refs/Closes + postmerge)
ready.description:
## Description

GAP: work was filed bd-only (intake/bd create default to zero GH calls) and PRs referenced bead ids (prx-xxx) not Closes #N, so GitHub issues were never created or closed (49 bd-only beads, 0 GH issues). FIX (no backfill, going-forward): (1) project new work units to GH at intake — either default 'prx intake --to gh' via a config (intake.project-to=gh) or make it the pipeline default; (2) the submit/publish-generated PR body auto-includes 'Closes #<gh>' for GH units and 'Refs <bd-id>' for bd units (submit body-template already does this — wire it into publish automatically); (3) auto-run 'prx submit postmerge <pr>' on merge so bd-tracked units close; (4) 'prx beads sync --domain=gh' reconciles. Enforced by the pipeline (forge owns the gh issue writes), not agent discipline. This issue itself was filed via 'prx intake --to gh' to prove the create half of the loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

a new work unit gets a GitHub issue automatically (or via one documented default); merging its PR closes the GH issue (Closes #N) or the bd issue (Refs + postmerge); 'prx beads sync --domain=gh' shows no bd-only drift for active units

ready.title: Capability-poor orchestrator: per-actor sub-agents, no ambient authority
ready.description: Ambient authority (Bash grants every capability at once) let the orchestrator do keeper/forge/publisher work directly (gh api PATCH, git push, publisher merge) and turned ownership/context errors into confusing raw failures instead of clean denials. Build a capability-poor orchestrator whose ONLY tool is delegate-to-actor; generate one Claude sub-agent per actor with a tool allowlist that is a PROJECTION of the policy table (codegen, same engine as README/rules). Each sub-agent runs in its owned context (keeper=its worktree+git, forge=gh, planner/executor/etc) with its own signing key (keymaker). Goal: 'orchestrator cannot do what sub-agents own' true by construction; ambient-authority leaks surface as denials. Sequenced AFTER prx-lrw + keeper-cross-worktree fixes.
ready.notes: Ephemerality: local salted worktrees + branches are execution scaffolding scoped to the SUB-AGENT's lifetime — created on agent start, destroyed on agent finish (like Workflow isolation:'worktree' auto-clean). The ONLY persistent state is the signed CAS artifact the agent hands off; branches are projections, never source of truth. The single branch that escapes to origin is keeper's published PR branch, materialized from the artifact at publish, GC'd post-merge. Corollary: ephemeral+salted+worktree-scoped branches mean there is never a persistent foreign branch checkout to collide with -> the keeper 'switch -C' gotcha cannot occur, and no manual 'git push origin --delete' cleanup is ever needed.

ready.title: Phase2.5: PR + merge as boundary artifacts (pr@pinned + merge/v1)
ready.description: The output boundary, symmetric with source@pinned at the input. A PR is an impure external object (GitHub review/CI/mergeability state), so FOD-pin it: <unit>:pr@pinned = {number, base, headCommit, state, mergeable, ci, approvals, threads}, content-hashed; isFresh detects drift (new push, CI flip, review). The merge is the TERMINAL signed attestation <unit>:merge/v1 (subject = merge commit, DSSE-signed by the merging actor) — the proof the chain landed (intake→merged-PR). Bookends the chain: issue(source@pinned) … push/v1 → pr@pinned → merge/v1; both ends impure-external-pinned, the middle pure+signed. Part of epic prx-dkc.
ready.notes: Serialized PR = git format-patch --cover-letter mbox = <unit>:pr@series CAS blob (cover letter = plan@ body + bead title = the proposal; patches = the commits; git am-applyable on base). Pure + transport-agnostic — GitHub PR is one rendering. Three PR-side artifacts: pr@series (serialized change+proposal, pure CAS), pr@pinned (external review/CI/merge state, FOD-pinned — not ours to serialize), merge/v1 (signed terminal).

ready.title: Session-open blocker messages: derive from the XState machine state, emit one real blocker+solution (pretty-printed)
ready.description: The 'Cannot open PRX session ... no local parity-chain unit' message is hardcoded (prxSessionNotProjectedLocallyMessage in session_open.ts) and lists a generic OR-list of 3 solutions (chain backfill / plan session --create / plan agent --create). The blocker check (hasLocalParityUnit, cli.ts ~4319) is an upstream function, NOT modeled in the session-open XState machine (machines/session-open.ts). ready.description:
Part of prx-zl3 (prx owns the toolchain). Today flake.nix devShell = pkgs.mkShell { buildInputs = [ pkgs.bun ]; } — provides the bun binary but NOT node_modules, so every fresh worktree starts test-broken until a manual 'bun install' (confirmed: this worktree had no node_modules; the cas test only passed because cas.ts has no external npm deps; repos.ts needed zod). worktrunk is still the only wt driver (prx tools wt wraps it; GH-1978 abstracts toward nix devShell/devcontainer/CI), so deps belong in the devShell/driver layer, NOT bolted into bootstrap_worktree.ts, and NOT a shellHook 'bun install' (that's the rejected bolt-in).

RECIPE (focused session — needs nix-build validation):
1. Add input: bun2nix (upstream github flake; pin a rev). Confirm the lib API for the installed/pinned version.
2. bun.lock is JSON (lockfileVersion 1) — bun2nix-compatible. Generate the lock-derivation mapping if the lib requires it (bun2nix CLI -> bun.nix), or use a lib fn that reads bun.lock directly.
3. devShells.default: add the bun2nix-produced node_modules derivation (symlink into the shell / set NODE_PATH) alongside pkgs.bun.
4. VALIDATE: nix develop -c bun test packages/prx/test/plan-store/cas.test.ts AND a zod-dependent suite (e.g. materialize) pass WITHOUT a manual bun install.
5. Confirm reproducibility: bun.lock change -> regenerate; document in CONTRIBUTING/flake.

NOT done in-session: speculative flake edits without nix-build validation risk breaking 'nix develop'. Do in a focused session with nix access.
ready.notes: EXTEND from devShell to RUNTIME — this is the prx-5el vehicle. DECISION: prx should USE THE FLAKES to provide native runtime deps, not internalize them in the bun --compile binary. bun --compile bundles the agent-SDK JS but NOT its platform native helper (@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64) — the compiled binary has no node_modules and the flake provides only bun (devShell), so the SDK's query() can't find its native helper at runtime ('Native CLI binary for darwin-arm64 not found' = prx-5el). PLAN: bun2nix-provide node_modules (incl. the agent-SDK + native helper) as a nix derivation, and wrap the prx binary in hm-module/fetch-release (makeWrapper: NODE_PATH / SDK native-binary path) so it resolves at runtime. Hermetic + fits the existing flake→fetch-release→hm-module distribution + same lever as bd/dolt (prx-zl3). Rejected: internalize via bun --compile --asset (fragile for spawned platform binaries). Also evaluate whether an agent-SDK bump (0.3.143→0.3.154, in the bun cache) makes pathToClaudeCodeExecutable fully bypass the native helper — would simplify. Verify both via prx-r2w.

The boundary resolves via git-dir/common-dir (bare subtree) not --show-toplevel (worktree root), so boundary path and walk path never intersect -> escapes to $HOME. FIX: bound discovery by --show-toplevel. Affects prx (worktree-everything).

(2) SCHEMA MIGRATION 0040 REQUIRES NEWER DOLT. bd 1.0.5 runs migration 0040_ignored_tables_also_nonlocal_tables which fails: 'Error 1146 table not found: dolt_nonlocal_tables' against the system dolt. So bd 1.0.5 cannot open existing DBs without a coordinated dolt upgrade. A bd bump is NOT safe standalone — bd+dolt must move together.

ready.description:
Hit live: 'prx home sync' from a feature worktree refuses with 'must run from the mainx worktree (got attach-beads). Use prx delegate next for feature work.' — but gives no path, forcing the operator to find mainx (../mainx) by hand. prx already resolves mainx internally (isMainxPath / materializeMainxIfMissing / result.mainxPath in cli.ts).

IMPROVEMENTS (ranked):
1. BEST — verbs whose work isn't tied to cwd contents (prx home sync = detach origin main + home update) should resolve the mainx worktree themselves and run there, regardless of invocation cwd. No cd, no refusal.
2. CHEAP — when a verb genuinely must run in mainx, the refusal should print the resolved path + the cd command, e.g. 'run from /…/mainx (cd ../mainx)'.
3. HELPER — add a 'prx mainx' (path-printer) so 'cd $(prx mainx)' works; optionally ship a shell alias. A CLI cannot change the parent shell cwd, so a printer + alias is the only real 'quick switch'.

Also: mainx can drift (was at 9344162 while main = 50a65bf post-merge); option 1 naturally re-syncs it.
ready.design:
OPERATOR DESIGN (2026-06-02): the mainx-resolution should be BUILT INTO the existing --repo flag, not a new mechanism. prx already has resolveTargetRepoCwd (GH-1689) — the slug->target-mainx resolver that 'prx plan session --repo' and 'prx triage session --repo' use. mainx path convention confirmed: canonicalMainxPathFromParsed = <wtRoot>/<name>.git/mainx (repos.ts:1408).

APPROACH: make mainx-required verbs (starting with 'prx home sync'/'home update') accept --repo <slug> and route through resolveTargetRepoCwd to operate against THAT repo's mainx, regardless of invocation cwd. So 'prx home sync --repo prx' resolves ~/.local/state/wt/worktrees/prx.git/mainx and runs there — no cd, no 'must run from mainx' refusal. Reuses the existing resolver; consistent with the established --repo UX.

Keep the cwd-based behavior as the default (run from mainx) but add --repo as the explicit, cd-free path. When --repo is absent AND cwd isn't mainx, the refusal should still print the resolved mainx path + 'cd' hint (cheap fallback).

FUTURE: 'prx home sync' / 'prx home update' are slated to be renamed/consolidated to 'prx update' — build the --repo/resolveTargetRepoCwd routing into that consolidation so it lands once, in the right place.

ready.title: Decision: adopt in-toto Archivista as attestation store, or keep the local DerivationStore ledger?
ready.acceptance_criteria:
- Discriminating question answered with a concrete PRX use case (or explicit 'not needed yet').
- If BUY: gitoid<->derivationId mapping strategy decided and recorded; adapter scoped against the attest.ts:52 seam; local-first deployment story (MinIO/local-dir + DB) addressed.
- If KEEP: decision recorded with the trigger that would reopen it (first real need for cross-artifact attestation discovery or graph policy).
- This ticket resolves to a one-paragraph decision note either way; not left open indefinitely.
ready.description:
DISCRIMINATING QUESTION (answer this first; it settles the decision):
Does PRX need attestation DISCOVERY / graph queries — 'given a commit or artifact digest, find every attestation referencing it as subject or material', cross-PR supply-chain traversal, policy gates over the graph?
  - YES  -> BUY Archivista. Subject-digest indexing + GraphQL graph traversal is its core competency and is expensive to build well.
  - NO   -> KEEP the existing ledger. PRX already persists, point-gets by id, and enforces publish-time idempotency.

WHERE ARCHIVISTA FITS (3 layers; it touches only one):
1. CAS (packages/prx/src/plan-store/cas.ts) — generic blob store for arbitrary content (plans/scout). Archivista is NOT a CAS ('only stores signed attestations'), so this layer is out of scope. The earlier 'build-vs-buy the CAS' framing was a category error.
2. Emission/sign/verify (slsa.ts, attest.ts) — pure projection to in-toto/Statement/v1 + slsa.dev/provenance/v1, DSSE-wrapped. Archivista CONSUMES this, does not replace it. Because PRX already emits canonical DSSE with bare-hex digests (slsa.ts:33-44, 'portable without translation'), envelopes upload to Archivista with ZERO format translation.
3. Persistence/retrieval — the ONLY layer in play. Today: DerivationStore (attest.ts:52) = append + get(derivationId), an idempotent flat ledger keyed by digestManifest. Point-get by the attestation's own id only; NO subject-digest index, NO graph traversal. Archivista's distinctive value is exactly this gap.

INTEGRATION SHAPE (if BUY):
- Seam already exists: attest.ts:52 injects Pick<DerivationStore,'append'|'get'>. Adapter = append -> POST /upload ; get -> GET /download/:gitoid. Drop-in at the existing injection point; no core change.
- OPEN ITEM (verify, do not assume): addressing mismatch. Archivista keys attestations by Gitoid (OmniBOR git object id of the envelope); PRX keys the ledger by derivationId (digestManifest of the manifest). Adapter needs a derivationId<->gitoid mapping, or carry derivationId as a subject/annotation. Confirm the mapping before committing.

OPERATIONAL COST:
- Archivista is a server: S3-compatible blob store (MinIO/S3, or local-dir option) + MySQL/Postgres for the metadata index. REST (POST /upload, GET /download/:gitoid) + GraphQL.
- Echoes the earlier ORAS-network-dep concern, BUT it lives at PUBLISH time, not in the offline/Nix dispatch hot path — so the network dependency is far more tolerable than ORAS-in-dispatch. A fully local-first deploy still means standing up MinIO/local-dir + a DB; non-trivial for a single-operator workflow.

REJECTED / OUT OF SCOPE:
- Archivista as a CAS replacement — rejected: it stores signed attestations only, not arbitrary blobs. cas.ts stays regardless.

Ref: https://github.com/in-toto/archivista
ready.design:
Two options:
(A) BUY Archivista — implement a DerivationStore adapter (append->POST /upload, get->GET /download/:gitoid) at the attest.ts:52 seam; gain subject-digest queries + GraphQL graph for free. Cost: S3 + Postgres/MySQL server at publish time; resolve gitoid<->derivationId mapping.
(B) KEEP the local ledger — no new infra; no graph queries. Sufficient if the need is sign/attach/verify/idempotent-store only.
Decision gate = the discriminating question. Do not adopt until a concrete need for subject-digest discovery or graph policy is demonstrated (YAGNI: server + DB is real operational weight for an unused capability).
ready.notes: Captured from a design discussion. Companion to prx-1ke (CAS read-only fix, closed). The CAS and the attestation store are SEPARATE layers — do not conflate. GH-1226 already settled the CAS default-home question; this ticket is solely about the attestation persistence/query layer.

Writing the redirect BEFORE the agent runs bd means bd resolves to primary -> connects to the shared server (3308) -> never spawns. Operator architectural call (agreed): prx should own the bd install + version pin, moving it out of bdelanghe/ai-home.

WHY (the frozen-bd bug is the failure mode of split ownership):
- prx-at2 happened precisely because ai-home pins beads transitively and 'prx home update' only bumps ai-home, never its beads input -> bd froze at a54ef8d (Apr 29, pre-PR#1731) for ~5 weeks. The repo that controls bd's version (ai-home, a personal home config) has no knowledge of prx's hard bd requirements.
- prx ALREADY owns the entire bd surface: 'prx tools bd' (policy wrapper), beads hydrate/sync, the dolt lifecycle verbs (prx-jkb), workspace_mode classifier, metadata_patch. bd is a de-facto prx dependency; the install is the one piece prx doesn't own — an inconsistency.
- 'Use prx on all repos' needs a self-contained toolchain. prx ships via Homebrew (bounded-systems/prx) + a nix home-manager module. If prx owns the bd pin, installing prx brings a KNOWN-COMPATIBLE bd — no dependency on ai-home being present or current.
- Enables a version-compatibility contract: 'prx X.Y requires bd >= Z', bumped + tested together.

HOW (migration):
1. Add a 'beads' input to the prx flake (this repo, bounded-systems/prx), pinned to a VERIFIED commit (4e8cedc — has PR#1731 git-root discovery boundary). prx flake already exposes homeManagerModules.default (nix/hm-module.nix) + packages.
2. Expose bd from prx's home-manager module (install the beads package) so consuming prx's module installs bd.
3. Remove the beads input + bd install from the bdelanghe/ai-home repo (avoid double-install/conflict).
4. Local ~/.config/home-manager already consumes prx's module (it sets PRX_* env); bd then comes from prx.

BONUS — folds in prx-6hd: once prx owns the install, prx's hm-module also owns BEADS_SHARED_SERVER_DIR (set it to $XDG_STATE_HOME/beads/shared-server), making prx the single owner of the beads runtime topology + XDG correctness.

REFRAMES prx-at2: the PERMANENT fix is 'prx owns + pins bd at a verified commit', NOT 'bump ai-home's pin'. The current local override (4e8cedc) is just the validation test.
